"Poh akan mencabar prosiding ini dengan bersungguh-sungguh dan akan mengambil segala langkah perundangan yang perlu bagi melindungi hak serta kedudukannya.”

Firma itu berkata prosiding sivil terhadap Poh bermula dengan permohonan 'citation' yang difailkan oleh Lim -- salah seorang daripada dua isteri Ta dan benefisiari harta pusakanya. Poh telah memfailkan permohonan untuk membatalkan permohonan 'citation' itu atas alasan ia remeh dan tiada merit.
Firma itu memaklumkan saman sivil Lim yang berikutnya, iaitu untuk menyingkirkan Poh, difailkan atas andaian bahawa permohonan 'citation' tersebut akan dibenarkan.
Firma itu menambah saman sivil berkenaan masih belum diserahkan kepada Poh dan tertakluk kepada hasil daripada permohonan Poh untuk membatalkan permohonan 'citation' tersebut.
Dalam perkembangan berasingan, pada 13 Nov, Poh minta dibicarakan bagi pertuduhan pecah amanah jenayah di bawah Seksyen 406 Kanun Keseksaan.

Beliau didakwa melupuskan 500,000 unit saham dalam Victoria Island Club Bhd, yang didakwa dipegang secara amanah untuk anak-anak Ta, dengan memindahkannya kepada Jennifer Kok empat tahun lalu tanpa persetujuan pihak yang dikatakan sebagai benefisiari.

Hakim Mahkamah Sesyen Rosli Ahmad membenarkan Poh diikat jamin RM400,000 dengan dua penjamin serta mengarahkannya melapor diri di pejabat Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia setiap bulan dan tidak menghubungi mana-mana individu yang berpotensi menjadi saksi sementara menunggu perbicaraan.
Poh berkata beliau tidak akan mengulas lanjut mengenai dakwaan tersebut memandangkan perkara itu sedang dibicarakan di mahkamah.
Kes itu ditetapkan untuk sebutan pada 8 Dis, manakala saman sivil dijadualkan untuk pengurusan kes pada 10 Dis.

Ta meninggal dunia ketika tidur pada 15 Jun 2024 pada usia 72 tahun. Mendiang mempunyai kepentingan perniagaan yang luas dalam sektor pembangunan hartanah, hotel, pusat peranginan, pembuatan dan kelab golf di Malaysia, China, Macau dan Hong Kong.
Beliau dipercayai meninggalkan harta pusaka bernilai jutaan ringgit untuk diagihkan kepada dua isteri dan tujuh anaknya mengikut ketetapan wasiatnya.
84d65590a9fe5734: KUALA LUMPUR: A student who was on his way to sit for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination fractured his left leg after the motorcycle he was riding collided with a car in Jalan Bangsar Utama 1 this morning.

0f00e2bbc2898924: DUBAI: Flydubai will resume direct flights to Tel Aviv next week, a company spokesman told AFP on Thursday, weeks after services to and from Israel were suspended following an attempt by a co-pilot to crash one of its planes.

be44507b799dbab6: PETALING JAYA: A disciplinary teacher at a secondary school in Tawau, Sabah, has been sentenced to two years in prison after being convicted of committing non-physical sexual assault against a 17-year-old student four years ago.
The Tawau sessions court sentenced the accused, 37, to a year in prison for the offence under Section 15(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, Harian Metro reported.

The teacher was charged with uttering lewd words to the victim as well as holding and pulling the student's hand for sexual purposes at the school's library around 9.20am on April 19, 2022.
However, the judge acquitted the accused of physically sexually assaulting another 17-year-old student, finding that the defence had raised a reasonable doubt.
He was accused of committing physical sexual assault against the victim at the library around noon on Feb 15, 2022.

f492acef8ba1d818: PETALING JAYA: The government needs to provide more attractive incentives and perks to encourage teachers to serve in rural areas, including reinstating the regional incentive payment (BIW) rate based on a percentage of their salaries, says the national teachers' union.

The National Union of the Teaching Profession (NUTP) said incentives should commensurate with the sacrifices made by teachers, especially those who have to be away from their families for long periods and bear additional costs to relocate.
NUTP secretary-general Fouzi Singon said the present implementation of the BIW at a fixed rate according to the service grade has made civil servants reluctant to accept postings in rural areas.
Before this, the BIW amount was 10% of a teacher's salary, he added.
"Reinstate the old regional allowance. Now, more and more people are refusing to (take up the postings) because it is not worth the cost they have to bear," he told FMT.

Yesterday, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim urged doctors, teachers, and other civil servants to accept postings in rural and remote areas, saying personal preferences should not leave communities without essential services.
Anwar said although the government was willing to adjust postings where reasonable, providing remote communities with access to healthcare remained a priority.
Fouzi also said the government should prioritise posting local residents in these areas to prevent civil servants from having to live away from their families.

He said better incentives and facilities should be provided to show the government's appreciation for their sacrifices, especially teachers who have to undertake dangerous journeys to reach their workplaces.
"Staff serving in rural areas should not be overlooked for various career advancement opportunities," added Fouzi.
1ec52ab2acfcb198: Travel giant Flight Centre Travel Group (FLT) says "a significant number of customer records" may have been accessed by "unknown persons" following a cyberattack.
The Brisbane-headquartered company said the incident affected a third-party accommodation booking system used by Flight Centre, Travel Associates, Cruiseabout, and some independent travel agents.
Its disclosure [PDF], filed with the Australian Securities Exchange today, added that it was aware that records were accessed, but cannot definitively say how many were exfiltrated.
Flight Centre is working with the supplier and incident response specialist Mandiant to establish the scope of the incident.

An initial review suggests most accessed records contained only customer names, some with basic travel information. A "very small percentage" may also include birth dates, email addresses, limited passport details, phone numbers, or, in rare cases, health or mobility information.
Flight bookings and corporate travel use separate systems and are unaffected, the company said.

"FLT values customer privacy and data security," the company said in its disclosure. "The company understands that an incident like this can be unsettling for customers who may be affected, and we apologize for any concern this causes."
Investigations remain ongoing, but FLT has already contained the attack, rotated keys and credentials, and increased system monitoring, it said.
The company said it would contact affected customers directly. Its brands continue to operate normally, and travelers should proceed with their plans.
Customers should independently verify unexpected messages about their bookings before clicking links, opening attachments, or sharing personal information.
The attack on FLT follows others that have hit booking systems in the past year, including those on Booking.com and BWH Hotels.
More recently, another Australian business, RMS Cloud, which provides booking software to travel and leisure companies, also acknowledged a breach that led to WhatsApp scams in late October.
Numerous reports of travelers being targeted with messages that contained their names and booking details hit local news outlets at the time.
Customers were sent convincing messages seemingly from the hotels they had booked, and according to Australia's National Anti-Scam Centre, the scams appeared to be financially motivated.

Muhammad Yahya Patel, vCISO and cybersecurity advisor for EMEA at Huntress, said attackers targeting booking systems is a "familiar supply chain story" that has a greater impact than simple data theft.

Speaking generally about the risks of exposed travel records, Patel said: "Unlike a compromised email address or phone number, a passport can't be changed easily or quickly. For affected customers, the practical risk extends well beyond the immediate breach.

"Passport details combined with names, addresses, and travel history create a comprehensive identity profile that enables document fraud, identity theft, and targeted social engineering that could persist for years." ®

fb38117fe35cda86: KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry will coordinate an integrated enforcement operation with relevant agencies following a viral video showing rats eating bean sprouts at a premises in Pudu Market.

In a statement, the ministry said the operation would involve the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, the Islamic Development Department of Malaysia (Jakim), the Immigration Department and Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL).

It said the operation would focus on compliance with premises hygiene standards, food handling practices, raw material storage, cross-contamination risks and the effectiveness of pest control measures.
Appropriate action would be taken against any non-compliance identified under the relevant laws, it said.
The ministry said it would also intensify monitoring and follow-up action to ensure corrective measures were implemented effectively and prevent a recurrence.
"The ministry will also strengthen coordination with DBKL to ensure that market cleanliness, waste management and rat population control are addressed comprehensively.
"The ministry, through the Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Federal Territories Health Department, has conducted an initial inspection at the premises and found that the issues raised were substantiated.
"Traders must ensure their premises are free from pests under Regulation 16 of the Food Hygiene Regulations," it said.
The ministry said compounds could be issued for offences, while premises that posed a risk to public health could be ordered to close immediately for up to 14 days under the Food Act 1983.
It reminded traders to keep their premises clean and free of pests, store food in covered containers, manage waste properly and carry out regular rat control measures.
"Any food exposed to rats or suspected of being contaminated must be discarded and must not be sold or used for food preparation.
"The ministry also advises consumers to choose clean food that is stored in covered containers and protected from pests," it said.
The ministry also advised consumers to wash raw ingredients under clean running water and cook them thoroughly before consumption.
Complaints can be lodged through the Public Complaints Management System at moh.spab.gov.my or at the nearest district health office.
Last week, a video showing rats roaming around and eating bean sprouts at a premises in Pudu Market went viral.
The video, taken from a TikTok livestream, was shared by a user on Threads, raising public concern over hygiene standards at the market.
The footage purportedly showed several rats on a container filled with bean sprouts, eating its contents.

2d18d5110e61fcdb: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will face 10-time champions Australia in the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup (SAS) final on Saturday.

Pakistan were leading 3-2 in the 32nd minute when Malaysia were awarded a penalty stroke. But Azrai Aizad's low flick was saved by goalkeeper Ishtiaq Abdullah Khan.
The 35-year-old Faizal said when Malaysia were trailing 4-2 with 10 minutes left, he told his teammates not to panic and not to give up.
"We fought hard for every ball and I was fortunate to score two goals in the space of a minute to level the scores.
"Although Pakistan regained the lead (5-4), we were awarded a penalty stroke (58th) and I calmly converted it.

Earlier in the day, Australia routed Canada 14-1 and South Korea edged the United States 2-1.
d6633dfbecea6483: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd has set a six-day target to restore the 275-kilovolt (kV) transmission line to Sabah's east coast after a transmission tower toppled in Ranau today.

Saadiah said Sabah Electricity personnel first cleared the main Ranau-Telupid road of hanging cables before carrying out emergency power restoration in stages.

Throughout the restoration period, she said electricity supply on Sabah's east coast would be generated using existing power stations in Sandakan and Tawau, supported by mobile generators sent to all affected areas.
"Sabah Electricity has succeeded in linking the east coast grid lines, boosting supply capacity and limiting electricity rationing to between one and two hours," she said.
Transmission tower T313 in Ranau toppled early this morning, affecting both transmission line circuits and disrupting electricity supply to Sabah's east coast.
Eight districts experienced a power outage at 6.04am.
ce20d0fd3fb76432: JERUSALEM: The centrist party of Gadi Eisenkot, who is trying to form the next Israeli government, and an allied left-wing party on Thursday announced they had agreed on a coalition deal.

The left-leaning Democrats are the second party to agree a coalition deal with Eisenkot's Yashar after the right-wing Israel Beiteinu party did so on Tuesday, marking a further step towards forming a government.

Eisenkot has until Dec 6 - a deadline which can be extended by 14 days - to form a government to replace caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc.
"Gadi Eisenkot, chair of Yashar with Eisenkot, and Yair Golan, chair of the Democrats, have agreed to sign a coalition agreement between the two parties," a joint statement said on Thursday.
It comes two days after the Democrats announced they were suspending talks with Yashar, with Israeli media reporting disputes over the allocation of ministerial portfolios.
Eisenkot, Liberman and Golan have a combined total of 36 lawmakers - far short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority.
Eisenkot's bloc also includes the Beyachad party of former prime minister Naftali Bennett which has 12 seats but is yet to sign a formal coalition agreement with Yashar.

Eisenkot's wide-ranging anti-Netanyahu camp has faced divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, or the Arab-majority lists, or whether to form a national unity government with Netanyahu's right-wing Likud.
The Democrats have been pushing Eisenkot for a coalition with two Arab-majority lists that achieved an unprecedented seat haul in the vote, in a bid to unseat Netanyahu.
The party viewed the four rounds of talks between Yashar and Likud unfavourably in recent days over the possibility of a unity government. No breakthroughs on that front have ostensibly been reached.
Liberman on Thursday warned that Netanyahu was trying to derail the government's formation.

"He will drag out negotiations over a 'unity' government until the last moment, look for a pretext to blow them up, and even if such a government is formed, he will try to engineer a crisis within a few months to drag Israel back to elections," added Liberman, a hawkish former aide to Netanyahu who has become a strident critic.

Liberman has refused to serve in a government that relies on Arab-majority parties and has instead advocated an alliance with the two ultra-Orthodox parties, despite his years of criticism of the community and the fact that the issue of ultra-Orthodox military conscription remains a thorny one.

9fee5aac53b74301: PETALING JAYA: The government does not plan on merging the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN) and customs department to establish a single tax agency, says finance minister Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar acknowledged that the single tax authority model was what countries like the UK, New Zealand and Singapore employed.
He said this differed from Malaysia's tax system, where LHDN manages direct tax collection while the customs department handles indirect tax collection.
"Both agencies fall under the oversight of the finance ministry, subject to different regulations and Acts. For now, the government has no plans to merge the two agencies.

"Nonetheless, the government will continue improving the administration of the country's tax collection system under both agencies to ensure greater efficiency in handling revenue leakage," he said in a written parliamentary reply.
Anwar added that Putrajaya continuously works with international organisations like the World Bank and local tax experts to improve the country's taxation model from time to time.
He was replying to Shafie Apdal (Warisan-Semporna) who asked if the government planned to create a single tax authority by merging LHDN and the customs department.
In August, Berita Harian quoted sources as saying that Putrajaya was considering establishing a single tax authority by consolidating the functions of LHDN and the customs department.
Officials from key agencies as well as the World Bank reportedly discussed the proposal during a meeting in June.

9ad2fb08fd7d39ed: BRUSSELS: Spanish central banking veteran Pablo Hernández de Cos was set to be chosen as the next head of the European Central Bank (ECB) on Thursday, a move that suggests policy continuity atop Europe's most powerful financial institution.

The widely telegraphed selection caps months of closed-door negotiations over seats on the ECB's six-person board, which will also see Germany grab the powerful chief economist role and France the position overseeing market operations.

Spain's De Cos, a former central bank governor and the current general manager of the Bank for International Settlements, will take over when current chief Christine Lagarde steps down early on Feb 7.
The way for him to replace her as the next ECB chief became clear on Thursday after the Netherlands decided to back him, effectively standing down its own candidate Klaas Knot.

The reshuffle comes as the ECB grapples with an Iran war-driven resurgence in inflation and worries that political turmoil in France could trigger broader financial market stress affecting other euro zone countries.

De Cos' appointment hands the top job to a southern European policymaker and ally of former ECB President Mario Draghi, reinforcing expectations that the central bank would ultimately use its firepower to contain any new sovereign debt crisis.
EU ambassadors were scheduled to meet at 2pm to launch the so-called written procedure in which capitals sign off on names for three top ECB jobs that will become vacant in the next six months.

The ambassadors will name De Cos for ECB president, and ⁠Laurence Boone and Markus Brunnermeier for the remaining two board seats. They are expected to become the head of the ECB's market operations and the institution's chief economist, respectively.
De Cos, 55, a trained monetary economist, has built a reputation for independent thinking anchored in economic theory, and pragmatism picked up over a decade served in policymaking roles.

He worked in various staff positions at the ECB and the Bank of Spain early in his career before making a rare jump to the policymaking level as governor of the national central bank, serving on the ECB's rate-setting Governing Council.

De Cos is a veteran of crises including Spain's banking sector bailout, the Covid-19 pandemic, and the post-pandemic inflation surge that forced the ECB into its fastest interest rate-hiking cycle on record.

While southern European policymakers are often considered "doves" favouring easier monetary policy, colleagues and ECB watchers say De Cos is pragmatic and a moderate who cannot be boxed into any such category.
ECB policy is decided by the 27-member Governing Council, meaning even the president has limited scope to steer interest rates single-handedly.
In any case, any dovish bias would only be relevant if inflation was slightly above target, and this year's surge in price pressures would force any ECB president to keep raising interest rates.
At 4%, inflation is now twice the central bank's target and policymakers speaking on and off the record appear unanimous that a rate hike in December is inevitable.

The path beyond is murky, however. Markets expect just one more upward move, given the recent retreat in oil prices and an expected decline in inflation from the spring, when statistical base effects start knocking year-earlier figures from the data set.

394e9f5b4e5d096c: Rackspace is shutting down its low-cost Spot cloud service after a security breach, giving customers two weeks' notice to move their workloads and retrieve their data.

In a notice posted on Tuesday, the cloud computing biz said its Rackspace Spot service will cease operations at 1700 Central Time (2300 UTC) on December 8. Any workloads still running at that point will be terminated, and customers will no longer be able to access their data.

"Following the recent security incident affecting Rackspace Spot, Rackspace has made the decision to wind down the service," the company said. "Spot customers are being notified with the wind-down timeline, instructions for retrieving their data and steps to secure their environments."
Customers will have to contend with the fallout from the breach while simultaneously trying to get their applications and data off the platform.

According to a customer notification seen by The Register, the attackers used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot over a period of almost 22 hours on November 17. Rackspace only learned of the intrusion the following day, after a customer raised the alarm.
The intruders impersonated legitimate users, created pods in customer Kubernetes clusters, gained access to stored credentials known as Kubernetes Secrets, and listed nodes and storage volumes.
"With that access, they could have read any Secret in an affected user's clusters, and any Spot API token or refresh token that user held," Rackspace told customers.

Rackspace has since revoked the affected tokens and sessions, removed the pods planted by the intruders, and changed the affected platform and storage keys. Customers must also reissue API tokens, download new Kubernetes configuration files, and rotate credentials stored in their clusters, including database passwords and third-party API keys.
Sirish Raghuram, co-founder and chief growth officer of Platform9, which co-developed Spot with Rackspace, shed some light on the root cause in a November 20 GitHub post.
"An observability system was breached using a compromised credential," Raghuram wrote. "This was obviously a critical error on our part and we are very sorry we let this happen."
Raghuram said the incident necessitated significant changes to the underlying infrastructure clusters, prolonging the outage.

Spot's selling point was cheap compute. The service operated an auction-based pricing model, allowing customers to bid for cloud infrastructure at a fraction of the cost of conventional on-demand instances. Rackspace advertised savings of up to 90 percent for customers willing to tolerate interruptions to their workloads. A permanent interruption probably wasn't what they had in mind.

Rackspace hasn't explained why it chose closure over recovery, revealed how many customers were affected, or said whether it will offer migration extensions. It did not respond to The Register's questions. ®

ec9fbbb151b965da: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where we’re thankful every time someone leaves a password sticky note on a monitor or fails to delete a terminated employee’s admin account. But neither of those common occurrences is what we’ll be talking about today. Instead, our subject broke the number-one rule of backups: you gotta keep ’em separated.

Our story comes courtesy of Da Li, who serves as global alliance manager at Info2Soft, a company that provides data protection and recovery software. At one point, a partner called him into a case where a Chinese vehicle parts manufacturer fell victim to a ransomware gang. Unfortunately, its backup was compromised too.

The manufacturer had religiously backed up its manufacturing execution system (MES) and SAP orders, inventory, and finance systems every night. There was even a green dashboard that showed the backup process had succeeded, and someone checked that every morning.

However, one Friday evening, crims broke into the network and found out that the backup server was joined to the same Windows domain as the rest of the network. The hackers found a plaintext password for the backup service account in a maintenance script on a file share and discovered that someone had used the very same password for a domain admin account.
So the first thing the crooks did was delete every restore point on that backup server. Then they started encrypting the production servers to ransom them.
“Every backup job had succeeded for three years,” Li said. “The failure was that the thing meant to save them could be reached with the same keys as the thing being attacked.”
The results were devastating. With the MES and SAP data both gone, the plant couldn't schedule production, ship parts, or track them.

By the time Li was called in, the plant had already resolved its ransomware situation. We don’t know whether it paid or not. The manufacturer did ask Li and his company to make sure that this couldn’t happen again.

Li’s fix was not radical, but it was instructive. He made sure that the company now keeps its backup system outside the production domain, uses unique credentials, and requires MFA to reduce the risk of unauthorized access even if a password is compromised. He also made sure that the company keeps at least one offline backup and runs a test restore quarterly to ensure it’s prepared for emergencies.®
354cbb8728340d15: UK public sector websites are directing visitors to gambling promotions through old links to defunct local enterprise partnerships (LEPs), research by digital consultancy Digital Royalty has found.
The consultancy identified 93 links across 79 pages on websites belonging to 26 public bodies.

LEPs brought together councils and businesses to promote economic growth in England under a coalition government initiative launched in 2010. Central government funding ended in April 2024, with their core functions transferred to local and combined authorities.

Among other things, Digital Royalty builds and looks after websites, which means chasing down old links. In August, it found that a link on Surrey County Council's website led to a former LEP address now displaying casino content. It went looking for more.
Digital Royalty founder Alex De Sousa said: "Slow is usually a sign of caution and diligence, but 31 months after the LEPs wound up, it's crossed into inefficient and dangerous."

The consultancy offered The Register four examples of websites run by the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS), Hull City Council, Parliament, and the Local Government Association. One example is a government page about the Digital Skills Partnership, originally published under an earlier incarnation of DCMS.

The page includes a link that appears to be for the Humber Digital Skills Partnership within the Humber LEP website, but in fact takes users to a site advertising "Independent Non GamStop Casinos UK – New Casino Sites Outside GamStop." GamStop is the self-exclusion scheme designed to help people restrict their online gambling, which makes the links more concerning than ordinary website clutter.
The same link appears on the Hull City Council website under a list of Joint Committees, Partnerships and Trusts where it appears as Local Economic Partnership (Humber LEP).

An old page for the Parliament website detailing the Department for Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy committee's Industrial Strategy report includes a footnote (135) that appears to be for the Business Central funding finder service, but takes the user to the "Highest RTP Non GamStop Casinos for UK Players."

The Local Government Association's (LGA) sustainability and waste route map included a link to the former York and North Yorkshire LEP website. The destination initially appeared legitimate but contained links promoting crypto casinos. The LGA now appears to have removed the link.

dd375bab412a437d: PETALING JAYA: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) reinforced its commitment to protecting electricity customers from rising global fuel costs through close cooperation with the government, supported by its sustained financial and operational resilience for the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026.

Against the backdrop of global fuel market uncertainties, including challenges arising from developments in West Asia, TNB remained focused on managing costs responsibly, supporting customers and sustaining the financial strength needed to meet Malaysia's growing energy requirements.
Putting customers first amid global fuel pressures

As global fuel cost pressures continue to affect energy markets, TNB and the government have undertaken coordinated measures to cushion customers from the impact of rising costs, while ensuring the continued reliability and sustainability of electricity supply.
While fuel cost fluctuations are reflected through the government-approved automatic fuel adjustment (AFA) mechanism, TNB has also taken proactive measures to support customer protection.

TNB is estimated to absorb up to RM150 million in AFA and retail charges following the expansion of the domestic customer protection threshold from 600 kWh to 800 kWh per month between September and December 2026, benefiting more than eight million, or up to 90% of domestic customers. These measures serve as an investment to forge long-term trust and regulatory stability, building the foundation for TNB’s sustainable returns.

This complements the government’s RM435 million injections from the Electricity Industry Fund (KWIE) to moderate AFA surcharges for May to August 2026. Customers had also received RM3.1 billion in AFA rebates between July 2025 and April 2026, reflecting the mechanism’s response to movements in global fuel costs.
Together, these measures reflect the close cooperation between TNB and the government in managing global fuel cost pressures while prioritising the interests and wellbeing of electricity customers.

Beyond cost mitigation, TNB continued empowering customers to manage their electricity consumption. The myTNB app enables customers to monitor their electricity usage, while its Energy Budget feature helps them plan and manage monthly consumption. The Time-of-Use (ToU) mechanism further provides eligible customers to manage costs by shifting usage to off-peak periods.

TNB president/CEO Shamsul Ahmad said the group remained committed to supporting customers while sustaining the operational and financial resilience required to deliver reliable electricity and prepare Malaysia's energy system for future growth.

“Our responsibility goes beyond keeping the lights on. It is about ensuring that households have reliable electricity for everyday life, businesses have the energy they need to grow, and Malaysia has a resilient electricity system capable of supporting its economic ambitions,” he said.
Keeping Malaysia powered

TNB continued to maintain dependable electricity amid increasing demand driven by industrial expansion under the Malaysia’s New Industrial Master Plan 2030 (NIMP 2030), the growing digital economy and rising investments in data centres.

Electricity demand grew by 8.3% year-on-year to 108.2 TWh, supported by increased consumption from the commercial and domestic sectors, alongside expanding economic activities and growing energy requirements from data centres, digital infrastructure and retail businesses.

Meanwhile, the System Average Interruption Duration Index (Saidi) improved to 34.90 minutes from 34.99 minutes during the corresponding period last year. This reflected TNB’s continued focus on operational performance and supply reliability, supported by preventive maintenance, network automation and operational readiness.
Advancing Malaysia’s energy transition ambitions

In support of Malaysia’s National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), TNB continued investing in critical energy infrastructure to accelerate renewable energy integration, enhance grid flexibility and ensure a reliable electricity supply as the nation transitions towards a low-carbon economy.

During the period, the group invested RM9.1 billion in reliability-related projects, supporting the development of a modern, resilient electricity system capable of accommodating growing demand and a more diversified energy mix.
Key initiatives include:
500 kV National Grid Backbone: Development of a 500km transmission backbone, targeted for completion by 2030, to strengthen grid connectivity and facilitate future energy integration.
Battery Energy Storage System (BESS): Commissioning of the 100-megawatt/400-megawatt-hour BESS in Santong, Terengganu, which was recognised as Malaysia’s first grid-connected, grid-forming BESS.

Regasification Terminal 3 (RGT-3): Collaboration with Petronas Gas Berhad to develop the facility in Lumut, Perak, enhancing long-term liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply resilience to support reliable electricity generation.

TNB also advanced regional energy connectivity through the Asean Power Grid (APG), including recent progress on the Vietnam–Malaysia–Singapore (VMS) cross-border electricity initiative, which aims to facilitate renewable energy exports from Vietnam through Malaysia to Singapore.

TNB remains committed in working closely with the government to ensure Malaysia’s energy transition is delivered in an orderly, affordable and secure manner. A stable and predictable regulatory environment will be critical to sustaining the investments needed for grid modernisation and renewable energy integration.
Creating values for communities and the nation
Beyond electricity supply, TNB continued contributing to Malaysia’s sustainable development through environmental conservation, education and community empowerment.
Throughout the period, the group channelled RM186 million towards community development and corporate social responsibility initiatives, including:
Education (RM133.2 million): Support through Uniten and Yayasan Tenaga Nasional, benefitting approximately 218,000 students.
Economic and social (RM23.3 million): School assistance, community electrification, disaster relief and Projek Mesra rakyat, benefiting 225,000 individuals.
Sports development (RM12.4 million): Hockey development and other sports initiatives, benefiting 54,000 athletes and sports enthusiasts.
Environmental protection (RM3.0 million): MyBrighter Green and other conservation initiatives.
Nation-building (RM14.2 million): Initiative supporting energy transition awareness, national unity, and technical and vocational education and training (TVET).
Additionally, RM10.6 million in zakat wakalah was channelled to over 60,000 asnaf beneficiaries.
Sustaining performance to deliver long-term value

During the nine-month period, TNB recorded revenue of RM53.9 billion, compared with RM50.1 billion in the corresponding period last year, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) stood at RM16.1 billion.
TNB’s resilient performance was supported by higher electricity sales, disciplined financial management and continued efforts to optimise operational efficiency across its businesses.

TNB’s achievements also gained recognition locally and internationally, including Brand of the Year 2026-2027 at the World Branding Awards, Power Utility of the Year at Enlit Asia, and Best Public Utility App for myTNB by PC.com Readers' Choice Awards 2026, reflecting its operational excellence, brand strength and customer-centric digital innovation.
Staying focused on Malaysia’s energy future
Looking ahead, TNB expects electricity demand to be influenced by commercial growth, digitalisation and expanding energy requirements, while remaining mindful of global fuel market uncertainties.

TNB remains committed towards prioritising investments aligned with the NETR, particularly grid modernisation, renewable energy integration and system readiness, to support Malaysia's economic growth and transition towards a sustainable energy future.

“TNB will continue balancing operational reliability, financial discipline and long-term investments to meet Malaysia’s evolving energy needs. Our focus remains on delivering secure electricity today while building a stronger, more sustainable energy system for tomorrow,” Shamsul said.
01fa59252bbea5d8: SIBU, Nov 26 — The landing of an empurau weighing over 12 kilogrammes at the premises of Sarawak wild fish supplier Jeferry Siew Seng Kwong here proves that the species is not merely an ordinary river catch, but a luxury commodity worth tens of thousands of ringgit.
Known scientifically as Tor tambroides, the fish, which fetches RM2,000 to RM2,500 per kilogramme in the international market, continues to cement its dominance in the exclusive culinary segment.

The iconic species is now sought after by high-end restaurants, wholesalers, and the elite in Hong Kong, China, and Singapore, as well as the Peninsular Malaysia market including Kuala Lumpur, Perak, and Penang.

Behind that extraordinary price tag, the journey of the “King of the River” begins far in the remote upstream areas before passing through a chain of fishermen, suppliers, and air logistics to reach the dining tables of high-income earners.
For Jeferry, 41, the business is not merely about chasing profits through trading exotic fish, but also ensuring that every bit of hard work by local fishermen receives a fair and lucrative return.

“This empurau has its own uniqueness with fine, tender, and sweet-textured flesh as well as a fatty belly, while its special aroma comes from its natural diet as it feeds only on wild forest fruits such as engkabang and ensurai.
“A large-sized fish can fetch tens of thousands of ringgit, even enough to buy an used car, depending on its weight and the market,” he told Bernama recently.
He said the uniqueness of the empurau, which inhabits fast-flowing upstream rivers, also lies in its growth period, which takes more than 10 years.

Fresh supplies are obtained directly from fishermen’s bases in the interior such as Ulu Kapit and Baleh, with the nearly 600-kilometre Batang Rajang river basin remaining the main habitat for various high-value freshwater species.

Close cooperation with local fishermen, including Leanard Anak Lenggie and Gamas Iban from Kapit, forms the backbone of his operational stability, which demands swift action as soon as the catch is brought ashore.
He said in the wild fish trade, there is no room for any delay as timeliness is the absolute determining factor in maintaining the freshness and highest-grade quality of the empurau.
He noted that demand for the premium species usually surges ahead of festive seasons such as Christmas and Chinese New Year to be served as a special dish for families and celebratory gatherings.

Apart from empurau, Jeferry’s business premises located at Jalan Long Bridge also supply various other freshwater species including patin buah, tapah, jelawat, semah, tengadak, terubuk, sebarau, giant freshwater prawns (udang galah), ketutu, and baung.
This variety allows his business to cater to the tastes and budgets of customers from various backgrounds, rather than relying on empurau alone.

Commenting on export matters, Jeferry said shipments outside Sarawak via air freight to maintain freshness also affect the selling price, in addition to requiring permits, veterinary documents, and shipping declarations.
His experience in managing shipping as well as import-export businesses has also been an advantage in handling documentation and logistics coordination to meet customer needs.

Ahead of the 13th Sarawak State Election, the Sibu native, who will cast his ballot in the Bukit Assek state constituency, hopes the potential of the river fisheries sector, particularly high-value species like empurau, will be given due attention by elected representatives as one of the state’s economic drivers.

He said continuous support in terms of infrastructure, basic amenities, and market access is crucial to ensure Sarawak’s river produce continues to bring greater benefits to fishing communities and the rural economy.

“I believe efforts to strengthen market access, transport facilities, as well as networks between operators and suppliers also have the potential to help this sector grow, thereby ensuring Sarawak’s river produce continues to secure a place in both domestic and international premium markets,” he said.
Bukit Assek is one of two state constituencies in the Lanang parliamentary constituency, alongside Dudong, involved in the Sarawak State Election.
The Election Commission (EC) has set this Saturday (November 28) as nomination day, followed by early voting on December 8 and polling day on December 12.
Get the latest news on the 13th Sarawak State Election via https://election.bernama.com/prn/sarawak/2026/. — Bernama
7d63a5daa9e95922: BEIJING, Nov 26 — The Badminton World Federation has approved sweeping changes to the formats of its major championships, expanding its flagship team competitions to 24 teams and introducing a group stage at the individual World Championships from 2027, Xinhua reported.
The Thomas and Uber Cups, badminton’s men’s and women’s world team championships, will also switch from best-of-five to best-of-three-match ties from 2028.
The Thomas and Uber Cups and the Sudirman Cup, the world mixed team championship, will adopt league stages followed by knockout rounds, replacing their existing group-stage formats.
Each team will play three league-stage ties at the Sudirman Cup, which will retain its best-of-five-match format, while teams at the Thomas and Uber Cups will each contest four ties.

Under a new points system, teams will earn one point for every individual match won, regardless of the overall result of the tie, with two bonus points awarded for a tie victory. The top 12 teams in each competition will advance to the knockout stage.
The system is designed to give greater significance to individual matches, even after the outcome of a tie has been decided.

From 2027, the individual World Championships will move from a straight knockout format to a group stage followed by knockout rounds across all five disciplines, bringing the competition closer to the format used at the Olympic Games.
The men’s and women’s singles events will each feature 48 players divided into 16 groups of three, while each of the three doubles events will feature 32 pairs across eight groups of four.
The format guarantees every player or pair at least two matches, with each national association permitted a maximum of four entries per event.

“These changes to our major championships are about creating stronger competition, opening the door to greater participation, and ensuring more members and players can share in badminton’s biggest moments,” BWF President Khunying Patama Leeswadtrakul said.

“Together with the introduction of the 3x15 scoring system, they form part of a broader vision to elevate our sport, deepen fan engagement, and strengthen badminton’s position as a truly global game.”
The BWF also confirmed several hosts for its major championships through 2030.

Mississauga, Canada, will stage the 2027 World Championships, while New Delhi will host the 2028 Thomas and Uber Cups. South Korea will stage the 2029 Sudirman Cup, with the host city yet to be determined, and Paris will host the 2030 Thomas and Uber Cups.
Beijing was announced last month as host of the 2027 Sudirman Cup. — Bernama-Xinhua
7388ff51f4ce2aca: THE HAGUE, Nov 26 — Former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte stands trial from Monday at the International Criminal Court in arguably the highest-profile case in the institution’s 24-year history.
Duterte is the first Asian former head of state to appear at the ICC and his trial comes as the court faces unprecedented global pressure, including sweeping sanctions from the United States.
Here are five key things to know about the blockbuster trial:
What are the charges?
Duterte faces three counts of crimes against humanity for indirectly co-conspiring to murder or attempt to murder alleged drug users or pushers during his so-called “war on drugs.”
He is charged with what ICC pre-trial judges called a “widespread and systematic attack against a civilian population” while he was mayor of Davao City and then president of the country.
The court will examine 49 incidents that resulted in the deaths of 76 people, with two attempted murders.
However, these incidents are “mere examples of the extent of the victimisation”, according to prosecutors.
The ICC said hundreds were killed during the time Duterte was mayor, with thousands then murdered when he became president.
Count one relates to 19 alleged murders carried out between 2013 and June 2016, when Duterte was Davao mayor.
The court will examine nine incidents.
Count two relates to the alleged murder of “High Value Targets” between July 2016 and July 2017 during Duterte’s presidency.
Five incidents will be considered, with 14 deaths.
Count three concerns 35 incidents during so-called “barangay (village) clearing operations”.
A total of 43 murders and two attempted murders is alleged.
How does the trial work?
The first day will be action-packed with spectators cramming into the public gallery and hundreds of Duterte supporters and victims expected to demonstrate outside the court.
Judge Joanna Korner will read out the charges to the 81-year-old, ask if he understands them and if he pleads guilty or not guilty.
The prosecution will make its opening statement (expected to last around three hours), followed by victims’ representatives (less than three hours).
Defence lawyer Peter Haynes has said he is “inclined” to respond after the prosecution and victims make their opening statements.
After opening statements, the prosecution sets out its case.
Around 100 witnesses are expected.
Victims’ representatives will then present their observations, followed by the case for the defence.
Duterte is innocent until proven guilty “beyond reasonable doubt.”
He can appeal any verdict.
How long will this last?
Probably several years.
The prosecution alone has been given 150 hours to present its case.
This does not include cross-examination by the defence.
Judge Korner has set a maximum of four hours sitting per day given Duterte’s age and fragile health.
There will also be regular breaks in proceedings.
After the trial has finished, the panel of three judges will issue their verdict “within a reasonable period of time.”
In the past, the ICC has taken more than a year to issue a verdict and the Duterte case is expected to take a long time given the complexity and stature of proceedings.
Is he fit to stand trial?
Duterte’s health has been a major topic in the run-up to the trial but judges have ruled him fit to take the stand, based on findings from an independent panel of doctors.
During his initial appearance, via videolink in March 2025, the former leader appeared dazed and disorientated, his speech barely audible.
His defence team has said he is suffering from “significant memory impairment” that means he often fails to remember his lawyer’s name.
He has been excused many times from appearing in person during pre-trial hearings, but Korner has said she expects him in court every day for the trial.
He appeared in court in person for the first time in September, seeming to follow proceedings and waving at the public gallery when the hearing ended.
What sentence does he risk?
At the ICC, sentencing is a separate procedure entirely.
Life imprisonment is extremely rare and time already detained is subtracted from the prison time.
The court could also order reparations for victims if Duterte is convicted.
This too is a separate procedure. — AFP
a03cc8632086aac6: BRUSSELS, Nov 26 — What will tomorrow’s Europe look like?
The answer may hinge on a looming year of back-to-back elections, with France at centre stage, that could change the face of the EU and potentially jam its decision-making.

Between now and the end of 2027, four of the European Union’s five largest countries will choose new leaders in contests marked by the rise of eurosceptic forces — groups wary of Brussels’ influence which seek to grant more power to individual member states.
It will be an unprecedented series of political tests for the bloc.
The most consequential vote takes place in April and May in France, where far-right leader Marine Le Pen is running in the lead.
Depending on the outcome in France and elsewhere, “what we risk is paralysis” in European decision-making, summed up one Brussels diplomat, granted anonymity to discuss the sensitive matter.
End of the Sanchez era?
The high-stakes electoral cycle kicks off this Sunday in Spain.
Shaped by heated debates over immigration and housing, that vote could end the era of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.
After more than eight years in power, Sanchez is one of the last remaining socialist leaders in the 27-nation bloc, often at odds with his counterparts including on migration and defence.
Most polls show him losing to conservative rival Alberto Nunez Feijoo.
The vote could also see the far right enter government for the first time since Francisco Franco’s dictatorship ended in 1975, with the Vox party seeking to play kingmaker.

Looking into next year, close attention will focus on Italy, where hard-right leader Giorgia Meloni faces a challenge on her right flank from former general Roberto Vannacci, an anti-migration hawk opposed to military aid for Ukraine.

And Brussels will be scrutinising parliamentary elections in Poland, set for a new showdown between the camp of pro-European Prime Minister Donald Tusk and that of nationalist President Karol Nawrocki.
At stake: two radically different visions of Europe, laid bare by a standoff surrounding Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal this autumn.
Next year will also bring elections in a host of smaller EU nations, such as Estonia –- an ardent backer of Ukraine which accuses Russia of targeting it with a campaign of sabotage.
Polls are likewise scheduled in Greece, Finland and Slovakia, where Prime Minister Robert Fico maintains friendly ties with the Kremlin.
Radical change
But no race is causing more concern in Brussels than the French presidential race.
Frontrunner Le Pen is pushing a vision for Europe in stark contrast to the one championed by President Emmanuel Macron over the past decade.
The National Rally (RN) leader has made clear she would shelve plans for further EU enlargement and pull the plug on funding for Ukraine.
Le Pen recently travelled to Brussels to make her case, vowing to pare back the European Commission to a “secretariat” serving member states and slash France’s contribution to the EU budget.
Celia Belin, of the European Council on Foreign Relations, said Le Pen’s “radical” policies on Europe “would be putting France on a collision path with EU institutions”.
Summit standoffs
The bloc’s top officials have yet to establish meaningful contacts with Le Pen, making it all the more difficult to predict the knock-on effects her election could have in Brussels.
It is an open question how discussions among the bloc’s 27 leaders might unfold during late-night European summits, if a victorious Le Pen decided to play hardball.
With German Chancellor Friedrich Merz already weakened in Berlin, would her election cause the EU’s decision-making machinery to grind to a halt?
Could commission chief Ursula von der Leyen – a frequent target of eurosceptics across the bloc – suffer the consequences?
Some in Brussels are already gaming out worst-case scenarios.
Others prefer to downplay Le Pen’s statements, arguing that if she comes to power she will have little choice but to work within the EU framework — as did Italy’s Meloni.
“Not everything has to be the end of the world,” countered one diplomat. “If there is a vacuum, other countries will fill the gap.”
Others caution against reading too much into polling, arguing eurosceptic forces may fail to convert momentum into votes.
But officials and diplomats AFP spoke to broadly agreed on one thing: the EU needs to bolster its ability to weather electoral shocks in the months ahead.
That effort starts now with hard-fought negotiations to agree the bloc’s next seven-year budget, and to secure funding for Ukraine through 2027. — AFP

ec36b65a3c23d86f: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today launched the National Security Policy 2026–2030, outlining Malaysia’s security priorities for the next five years, with a new strategic focus on cybersecurity and technology.

The policy takes into account changes in the geopolitical landscape and increasingly complex traditional and non-traditional security threats, aiming to strengthen the country’s preparedness against emerging challenges.

Anwar said the policy adopts a Comprehensive Security approach, covering politics, the economy, society, the environment, public safety and technology, supported by collaboration between government agencies, the private sector, academia, non-governmental organisations and the public.
“Our approach and outlook towards security threats have changed.
“We are no longer dealing solely with conventional forces or threats originating from other countries or within the region.

“This underscores the need to strengthen our cybersecurity capabilities, including investing in training and developing infrastructure to address new and increasingly unpredictable threats,” he said in his speech.

Anwar said security threats were no longer confined to conventional conflicts between countries, with cyberattacks increasingly targeting financial systems, defence networks and critical infrastructure.
“The National Security Policy takes into account the perspectives of previous policies, but I believe its strength lies in its ability to anticipate and address new issues and challenges,” he said.
He urged relevant ministries to consider setting up dedicated units to strengthen national capabilities, particularly in cybersecurity, while improving coordination between agencies.

55fdee707b66a112: Microsoft has released an out-of-band hotpatch to fix a bug in November's Windows Server 2025 security update that could crash some servers when an IPv6 route expires.

The patch for the patch, KB5138318, addresses crashes on systems with Router Advertisement (RA) enabled that receive time-bound IPv6 routes. When a route timer expires, affected servers can halt with error 0x139 (KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE).
Issued on November 25, the corrective update takes effect without requiring a restart, according to Microsoft.

KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE means the kernel has detected corruption of a critical data structure and stopped the system. Microsoft has identified route-timer expiry as the trigger but hasn't explained the underlying coding fault.
Good to see the operating system being protected against the impact of the corruption. Less good for administrators wondering why their servers have suddenly misbehaved.

Lansweeper puts Windows Server 2025 at 7 percent of the servers it monitors, compared with 32 percent for Server 2022 and 33 percent for Server 2019. Only systems with the affected hotpatch and networking configuration are implicated.

Microsoft's Windows Server updates have not gone well over the last few months, with out-of-band updates issued in September, October, and November. An out-of-band update to deal with a problem introduced in a hotpatch (in this case, KB5131077) therefore carries with it a certain sense of inevitability.

Hotpatches are a way of getting OS security updates on a Windows Server without requiring a restart and so are, in theory, a boon for administrators keen on maximizing uptime. According to Microsoft, in addition to faster installations and better protection, there is "lower workload impact with less need to restart your machine."
Avoiding a planned restart is less of a selling point when the alternative is an unplanned crash. ®

c9d929f7e8b12eb6: Much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it.

A new study led by Jevan Yu at MIT focuses on peatlands—environments like bogs and fens where organic matter accumulates into thick layers of material. Some 600 billion tons of carbon are held in these vast stores of peat, which is more than you can find in all the world’s living vegetation, the researchers note.

Because these areas are permanently inundated, any oxygen in the water is quickly used up, leaving the job of decaying all that organic matter to anaerobic bacteria that work much more slowly and don't digest everything. So instead of seeing organic carbon turning into the CO2 gas released by aerobic bacteria, in peatlands, a subset of it gradually turns into methane gas. Methane is an even more potent greenhouse gas than CO2 itself and ultimately gets oxidized into CO2. That means there’s a little trade-off from peatlands—most of the carbon they have is kept out of the atmosphere, but the carbon that does escape does so as methane.

db125f4552756b9b: <!--kg-card-end: html--> Grand Theft Auto VI is 2026’s breakout entertainment event. By the numbers, it made roughly $3.79 billion in revenue at launch, outpacing the lifetime earnings for megahit films like Avatar, The Odyssey, and Avengers: Infinity War. PlayStation called it their biggest launch of all time with over 39 million players on the platform alone. It’s the center of the current cultural zeitgeist, whether it’s because of the game’s controversy, music, love story, cultural legacy, or its accolades.

Entire households are playing GTA VI with one slight hitch: unlike movies, TV shows, or even books you can read side by side, a single-player, 40+ hour experience is tough to enjoy when you live together.

For some couples, the solution has been using more than one console or even multiple copies of the game. Married couple Meagan Kelley and Kyle Prahl typically switch between playing different games in the same room, or the same platforms in different parts of the house. The two are parents who find time to game after putting their son to bed. “The nice thing about having really young kids is they do go to bed super early,” Kelley told me. “Usually [my son] goes down and is asleep before eight, so then that's kind of like our prime gaming time.” The couple often plays different games in the same room, but for GTA VI “we're playing separately, so that kind of sucks because it's like we don't get a lot of time for each other,” Kelley said.

Although some men online have whined about Grand Theft Auto VI’s central romance, complaining about doing favors for their in-game girlfriend Lucia (“cuck simulator” being one common refrain), Kelley says the benefits to her real-life relationship are only positive. “It's funny that there's so much online discourse about GTA splitting up relationships and stuff when it's like something that can bring Kyle and I closer,” Kelley said. “Especially as we become parents and need to have more perspective on making sure that we're making time for ourselves.”

Dividing up time to play and sharing their experiences, she said, adds a new dimension to their mutual hobby. “When we are together taking care of our kid or having conversations, it's almost like book club,” Kelley said. “We share the different ways that we're experiencing the game with choices and stuff like that.”

Justin Massongill, another GTA VI player, and his wife recently had their second child. “She's taken on a lot,” he said. He bought the game for her, giving her priority to play so she could de-stress.

Massongill watched his wife play the first hour of the game; the next morning, he started his own. “We're kind of trying not to look too much at the other player's screen,” he said. “I don't want to, you know, get spoiled on things. But it's also such a massive game that what are the chances that we're going to see the same thing in the first place?”

<!--kg-card-begin: html--> <!--kg-card-end: html--> Madeline Blondeau and her fiancée decided to buy their copy of Grand Theft Auto VI together. The $80 price tag wasn’t so bad between the two of them; they downloaded the game, knowing that even with a PlayStation 5 and a PlayStation 5 Pro, they’d have to divvy up time between their single copy.

“We have been alternating our schedules,” Blondeau said. Her fiancée wakes up at 5 a.m. to start her IT job. Blondeau’s shift starts around 10 a.m. “We've sort of worked this out—me playing while she is working, and then her playing while I am finishing up my shift, trying to tiptoe around spoilers.”

Even as a queer couple, there’s an equality and care for each other in the experience Blondeau finds reassuring. “I think there's these very gendered expectations in relationships in terms of who games, who is the gamer of the household,” Blondeau said. You even see it in Grand Theft Auto, she adds, where Jason, the game’s male protagonist, will be the one with a controller in his hand. “Breaking down the gendered expectations of who is the gamer in the relationship really opens up a whole avenue for not getting into fights with your partner over video games,” Blondeau said.
“It feels like two people who figure their shit out, working out equitable time to experience something they've liked their whole lives, and talk about it.”

This past weekend, Blondeau’s fiancé left to grab groceries. She came back with something extra: the Grand Theft Auto trilogy for Nintendo Switch, a consolation prize for whoever wasn’t playing their shared copy of GTA VI. “I was in the mood to play Vice City,” her partner said. “We can trade off."

Then she made comments about SNP leader and Scottish First Minister John Swiney.

“Last night the SNP angered anti-AI campaigners by posting AI-generated GTA memes on its social media despite huge concerns about the impact of AI and AI data centers on artists, workers, and the environment,” Mackay said in the parliament session. “Does the first minister understand why people are concerned about his government’s approach to AI and the big companies behind it.”

The SNP deleted the memes and Swiney apologized. “First of all, let me say that I don’t want to offend anyone by anything that we get up to, so if I’ve offended anyone about that, I’m sorry about that. It was not my intention,” Swiney said in the Scottish parliament. Then he said he shared concerns about AI but defended the technology’s use for healthcare.

There will be more bad posts like this. Grand Theft Auto VI hasn’t been out for even a week and the memetic landscape around it will shift and change. We don’t even know what the dominant memes for the game are yet, let alone the innovative ways posters will iterate on them. Rest assured, however, that the governments of the world are watching and waiting to post their own variations and make it all cringe.

e4e7613e7956273e: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today emphasised the importance of diplomacy in addressing regional security challenges, stressing the need to maintain strong ties with neighbouring countries.

Speaking at the launch of the National Security Policy 2026 to 2030 today, Anwar said Malaysia must prioritise diplomacy and maintain good relations with its neighbours to address regional security challenges while ensuring its own defence capabilities remain strong.

This includes maintaining diplomatic engagement with Myanmar to address longstanding issues surrounding the repatriation of refugees from Myanmar in Malaysia, as well as pushing, through Asean, for a Code of Conduct on the South China Sea.
“When my fellow ministers discuss whether we should maintain good relations with Myanmar’s government, my answer is yes.
“Why? Because it is necessary to resolve many of the problems we are facing.

“The issue involving 200,000 Myanmar nationals in Malaysia cannot be resolved by international organisations or foreign countries, regardless of how extensively they discuss the matter. We have to resolve it ourselves,” Anwar said.
Anwar said Malaysia is also seeking assurances from Myanmar that the safety of those being repatriated would be guaranteed and that their situation could be monitored upon their return.

He stressed that the government was not sending them back to face harm, adding that failing to address the issue would place a greater financial burden on Malaysia and potentially worsen public frustration and security concerns.
Malaysia has faced international criticism over its approach to the refugee issue involving Myanmar.
“Sometimes, refugees are unable to find employment, and this can contribute to an increase in crime-related issues, for example.
“That is why, in my view, discussions on national security must also take into account the wisdom of maintaining good diplomatic relations with neighbouring and regional countries,” Anwar said.

On the South China Sea dispute, Anwar stressed that Malaysia would continue to pursue diplomatic negotiations with China through Asean while strengthening its defence capabilities to safeguard the country’s maritime interests and sovereignty.

He said that Malaysia would continue working with Asean to pursue negotiations with China and push for the finalisation of a South China Sea Code of Conduct, which he said should be anchored in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea 1982.
“I am not suggesting that Malaysia does not face problems.
“Malaysia is a maritime nation, and we have issues involving our neighbours and our maritime boundaries.
“However, the existence of these issues does not mean we are enemies or that they should lead to tensions in our bilateral relations,” Anwar said.
He added that Chinese Premier Li Qiang had also agreed to step up efforts towards finalising the Code of Conduct during the recent Asean meeting.
Asean and China missed their 2026 target for concluding the code but have reaffirmed their commitment to expedite the talks, with no new deadline set.
“Our Navy must always be prepared. We have consistently reminded them that defence is a major responsibility, and they must remain vigilant and maintain control over our waters.
“But we have not experienced the kind of confrontations seen in the Philippines, nor have we been involved in similar incidents.

“I have chosen the diplomatic path, although I agree with the calls made by the defence minister and the Defence Ministry for us to strengthen our capabilities and readiness to safeguard our national interests,” Anwar said.

The launch of the National Security Policy 2026 to 2030 was also attended by Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, and National Security Council director-general Datuk Raja Nushirwan Zainal Abidin.
d0bc4ea904511dad: The UK government is working "around the clock" on contingency plans for Capita contracts after the outsourcer's CEO quit and its shares plunged, a Cabinet Office minister told MPs.

Capita announced plans this week to raise around £190 million through a share issue in the first half of 2027 after warning of sharply lower profits and further costs linked to its Civil Service Pension Scheme (CSPS) contract.
The outsourcer "should be absolutely ashamed of its performance" on the £239 million contract, Sally Jameson, parliamentary secretary in the Cabinet Office, told MPs on Tuesday.
"We have seen evidence that it has stepped up in recent months and begun to rectify the problem, but it is inexcusable that it let the situation get to this point," she said.
Adolfo Hernandez stepped down as CEO with immediate effect on Monday, with finance chief Pablo Andres taking over. Shares fell around 70 percent following the announcement.
In the House of Commons, Jameson was asked about the government's plans if Capita were unable to carry out the remainder of its contract given the outsourcer's performance on the CSPS.

"On contingency planning, it is important that we stabilize the situation and that Capita can continue to deliver the pension scheme. However, the government is working across departments, as we do in relation to all strategic suppliers, to ensure that the relevant contingency plans are in place. People are working around the clock on that," she said.
Jameson said contingency planning for the pension scheme was already underway before Monday's announcement, describing it as standard practice for major government suppliers.
She told the Chamber that the Cabinet Office was "currently arranging to meet the new CEO in the coming days" following Hernandez's departure.

The Register first exposed problems with Capita's CSPS portal last December. The site, serving 1.5 million current and former public servants, rejected login details even for newly created accounts, contained broken and circular links, and displayed dummy text.

In January this year, the Cabinet Office was forced to promise "interim support measures" for the CSPS following Capita's botched takeover, including 150 additional government staff to clear the backlog in cases.

Speaking in Parliament, Conservative MP Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, chair of the Public Accounts Committee, said there had been "some tragic and dreadful cases" since Capita took over administration last December.

"I heard of one poor lady who was living on benefits because she could not get the bereavement payments she needed after her sister's death. I have heard of a member of parliamentary staff, not far from this Chamber, who is having to delay his retirement by a year because he cannot even get a statement from the scheme."

The government has withheld nearly £10 million in contractual payments over Capita's performance. It is currently locked in negotiations over further penalties following the appointment of an auditor, first revealed in July. At the time, Hernandez apologized for Capita's performance but refused to commit to further compensation.
The National Audit Office and Public Accounts Committee have both launched probes into Capita's handling of the CSPS and its appointment as a contractor.

In February, The Register revealed a legal challenge to the government's award of the separate Synergy shared services contract to Capita. The deal covers HR and finance services across four Whitehall departments and associated arm's-length bodies. Rival bidder Sopra Steria, which owns incumbent provider SSCL, alleges Capita's bid was abnormally low and its proposed staffing raised concerns about delivery. Capita and the Department for Work and Pensions, which led the procurement, deny the allegations and say the competition was fair and open. Capita values the contract at £370 million.
The Public and Commercial Services Union is now calling on the government to scrap Capita's shared services contract with the DWP, citing the outsourcer's troubled handling of CSPS. ®
b5cf4135eb16ab65: MOSCOW: Russian oil major Lukoil's withdrawal from international markets was driven by politics rather than the company's own choice, co-founder Vagit Alekperov said on Thursday in his first public comments on the planned sale of its overseas assets.
Lukoil, Russia's second-largest oil producer, announced the sale of its international portfolio last year after the US imposed sanctions on the company in October 2025 over Russia's war in Ukraine.
Russia's largest oil producer, Rosneft, has not put its foreign assets up for sale.
The state-controlled company, which is also subject to US sanctions, is headed by Igor Sechin, a long-standing ally of president Vladimir Putin.
Germany placed Rosneft's local units under trusteeship in 2022 after the war upended Berlin's decades-long energy ties with Russia.
Lukoil's international asset sale is the most consequential action so far by a Russian company in the wake of Western sanctions over the Ukraine war, which started in February 2022.
"Lukoil did not make the decision to withdraw from international markets on its own. This was driven more by political factors," Alekperov told Russian state TV programme Vesti.
"However, we are not shutting the curtain completely. We still hope to return," he said.
Alekperov was Lukoil's CEO for nearly 30 years before he stepped down in April 2022 after some Western countries introduced sanctions against him.
US billionaire Todd Boehly said on Wednesday he had signed a deal with Lukoil for a consortium that includes the US International Development Finance Corp (DFC) to acquire the international assets.

Lukoil's overseas portfolio, which spans about 40 countries and includes oilfields in Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and 9 other countries producing about 350,000 barrels of oil per day, is valued at around US$16 billion, two people familiar with the terms of the deal said.

021d7193e8027ab4: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The Dewan Rakyat today passed the Supply Bill 2027 via a voice vote at its third reading, capping weeks of committee-stage debate.
This is Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s fifth and biggest federal budget, although development spending is still lower than the record allocation announced for 2023, at RM97 billion.
Deputy Speaker Datuk Seri Ramli Mohd Nor declared the Bill approved late this afternoon after the Ministry of Youth and Sports wrapped up the final round of debates.
No Opposition MPs rose to call for bloc voting.
As a voice vote does not record a head count, the outcome does not show how many MPs backed the Bill.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, was present in the House alongside some senior ministers.

The RM459.8 billion spending plan comes to RM510 billion when investments from government-linked investment companies, statutory bodies, Minister of Finance Incorporated companies and public-private partnerships are factored in.
It passes ahead of a potential general election that might be called next year.
Of the RM459.8 billion direct federal allocation, RM376.8 billion is earmarked for operating expenditure while RM83 billion goes toward development.
Today’s uncontested vote was largely telegraphed following a Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) inked on October 29 between the Anwar administration and 13 MPs.

The CSA, announced the same day the Bill cleared its policy stage, was signed by six Bersatu MPs led by party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, six former Bersatu MPs and Muda’s Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.
Under the pact, the signatories will back the budget and Anwar’s administration in return for the same constituency allocations as government backbenchers.
The agreement also covers institutional reforms, including limiting the prime minister’s tenure to two terms and separating the powers of the attorney general and public prosecutor.
Anwar had previously confirmed that constituency allocations for the 13 signatories would be disbursed upon the Supply Bill’s final approval in Parliament.
